messages:
maria: Hey team — escalation from AcmePayments. After a feature deploy they hit a bunch of 429s for checkout traffic, ~10% of requests failing. They say they use a single API key per service and route through a corporate NAT. Customer expects project-level quota to be applied first, not the NAT IP. Any quick ideas?

samir: Hmm. Two likely things: (1) NAT means many services share one public IP so IP-based quotas can trigger earlier, (2) we also recently changed org-level fallback behavior for reserved pools. Did they give examples of failing requests (headers/logs)?

maria: Provided a sample curl and response body. Pasting sanitized response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "quota_scope": "ip",
  "quota_bucket": "nat-88-192",
  "retry_after": 12
}
```
They say the API key is for project "payments-prod" which still has quota left.

samir: That quota_scope: ip is the clue. Our attribution order is: API key > project > org > ip (usually), but if we detect proxy/nat heuristics or missing key metadata we can fall back to ip attribution. Two things to check: (A) whether the proxy strips/changes the Authorization header causing requests to be unauthenticated, (B) whether the proxy is injecting a different API key header or rewriting X-Forwarded-For.

kevin: Also check the request received by our edge: `x-auth-method` and `x-attribution` headers in the edge logs. If the edge couldn't validate the key it will attribute to IP and not to the key's project.

maria: Customer pasted server-side log excerpt: 
```
edge-log: id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/generate src=52.34.11.9 auth=ok key=sk-live-*** project=payments-prod quota_attrib=ip nat_detected=true
```
They claim auth=ok but still quota_attrib=ip and nat_detected=true. Confusing.

samir: auth=ok + quota_attrib=ip means our policy saw the key but a higher-priority pool (ip-based burst pool / org pool exhaustion rule) was selected. That can happen if the project is under a restrictive per-project rate and there's an org-level automatic fallback policy that shifts attribution to the shared NAT pool to protect project budgets. I'll check policy audit.

oncall-bot: Policy audit: route=payments-prod fallback_policy=org_fallback(enabled) ip_pool=nat-88-192 active_burst=3600s.

kevin: If org_fallback is enabled we move requests into org or ip buckets when project throughput exceeds threshold. But that should still preserve billing attribution to project unless the config `attribution_on_fallback=false`. Check their org settings for "charge_on_fallback" flag.

maria: On the call now with customer — they say they never enabled any org fallback. Is that a default?

samir: Not usually. But we rolled a change that enables org_fallback for orgs with shared NAT warnings. The logic flips if our NAT heuristics detect >X distinct keys behind a single IP. That could have auto-enabled fallback to prevent noisy neighbors. It may not show in UI until a later sync.

kevin: Repro steps to confirm: ask the customer to send two parallel requests: one with a header `X-Debug-Attribution: 1` so we return full attribution info, and one small test that increments their project counter. We can then see whether the project counter increments or the IP bucket increments. Use curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." -H "X-Debug-Attribution: 1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

maria: Sent that to them. They returned: 
```
{"attribution": {"by":"ip","ip_bucket":"nat-88-192","project":"payments-prod","project_counted":false}, "note":"project quota unchanged"}
```
They also included a screenshot of their proxy config — it terminates TLS and reissues requests to us using a service account that appends their own Authorization header (the same key) but does not preserve client-identifying metadata.

samir: There it is. Because the proxy is rewriting connections and not forwarding original client certificate or X-Forwarded-For reliably, our NAT heuristics kicked in and we moved to ip attribution. Two remediation paths: (A) ask customer to enable forwarded client IP propagation (X-Forwarded-For) and set `preserve-auth: true` so we can see original key per upstream connection, or (B) we can flip their org config `charge_on_fallback=true` so billing/quotas still prefer project attribution even when fallback is active (temporary).

kevin: Short-term I recommend enabling `charge_on_fallback=true` for AcmePayments so they stop seeing 429s for the project. Medium-term they should update proxy to preserve original client identifiers. I'll file an internal config change and patch the org flag.

maria: I've applied `charge_on_fallback=true` on their org and told them to re-run the test. They retried and reported no more 429s on the small test, large traffic test tomorrow.

samir: Follow-ups: (1) Add to KB a note about NAT auto-fallback heuristics and `charge_on_fallback` flag, (2) Ops to surface a warning in Console when NAT heuristics auto-enable fallback so customers aren't surprised, (3) Support to include `X-Debug-Attribution` in repro checklist.

maria: Thanks — I'll close the escalation after the tomorrow load test and add KB link to ticket. :thumbsup:
